drills.title: Transport, hotels and plans
drills.instructions: Read the message and type one word in each numbered gap. Then answer questions 5 and 6.

questions.explanation: The expression going to introduces the plan.
Use does to ask a present-simple question with he.
Don’t have to means there is no requirement.
Both if and whether introduce a yes/no question when you ask someone to check.

questions.prompt: Boarding closes at 7:10. The coach leaves at 7:15. Which arrival gives you two minutes before boarding closes?
questions.explanation: Count back two minutes from the boarding deadline of 7:10.

questions.prompt: Check-in starts at 2 p.m. Early guests may leave bags at reception. What can Nina do if she arrives at noon?
options: Check in if she leaves her bag at reception.
Leave her bag and wait to check in.
Go to her room while reception keeps her bag.
questions.answer: Leave her bag and wait to check in.
questions.explanation: The notice allows bag storage before check-in, which starts at 2 p.m.

cloze.title: Before we leave
cloze.text:
Hi Jules,

We’re going [1] take the early coach because our seats are already booked. Does Milo have his ticket on his phone, or [2] he need to get it at the station? If you bought your ticket online, you don’t have [3] print it. Could you check [4] breakfast is included in the room price? If it costs extra, we’ll eat at a café.

Thanks!
Nina

illustration.alt: Two people arriving at a small performance hall

drills.title: Experiences and invitations
drills.instructions: Type one word in each numbered gap. Use the verb in parentheses where you see one. Then answer questions 5 and 6.

questions.explanation: Use the past participle been for experiences of visiting or attending a place or event.
Last June names a finished time, so use the past simple.
Use the past participle after I’ve never.
Would you like to is a polite way to invite someone to do something.

questions.prompt: Rina replies, “I can’t make Saturday. Are you going again on Sunday?” What is she doing?
options: Accepting the invitation for the original day.
Asking whether she can go on a different day.
Turning down the festival because it’s outdoors.
questions.answer: Asking whether she can go on a different day.
questions.explanation: She can’t go on Saturday but asks about another day.

questions.prompt: Mo later says, “The film was good, but we had to move closer to understand what people were saying.” What was the problem at first?
options: The dialogue was hard to hear.
The film was too difficult to follow even after they moved.
Their new seats were too close to the screen.
questions.answer: The dialogue was hard to hear.
questions.explanation: Moving closer helped them hear the people speaking.

cloze.title: A movie in the park
cloze.text:
Hi Rina,

Have you ever [1] (be) to an outdoor film festival? I [2] (go) to a concert in that park last June. I’ve never [3] (see) a movie outdoors, so I’m excited. Would you like [4] come with us on Saturday?

Mo

interview: How do you usually travel to school?
What do you like to do on weekends?
Have you ever been to a live show?

followUps: What do you have to bring?
